title: Parade pay and long carnival days with Grand Isle trips
summary: Funerals paid $3 and parades up to $5, while carnival paid $10 a man.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. $3 for a funeral and most you could get is $5 for a parade. Now like on the place for the bulls, not the bulls to El Noro, but we paid us $10.
Is that for carnival? That's carnival. Yeah.

Paid us $10 a man. For all day long? That's all day long from 6 to 6. Yeah, from 6 to 6. 6 in the morning? 6 to 6. We go up there all in the morning and bring them all around to pick up the gang. And then we start up. What do you mean? You're tired after that? Oh man, you're tired. I guess you're tired. Then walk up there and—no, we walk coming this way, then we walk back. That's two trips. That's about 60 some odd blocks, ain't it? Oh yeah, the time they go all around? Yeah. Way up on the other side of the park. Yeah, on the other side of the park. Yeah. Audubon Park. Yeah. Yeah. Oh man, that was terrible. I stayed there for three, uh, four seasons. Yeah, but it was time. When you finish there, you've got enough. Then I leave there, and the truck be waiting for me to go down to the islands some ways. I come here in these little boy, jump over the truck, go to the islands, say, go down to Shell Beach, go down to Muzzle the River. Muzzle the River. Muzzle the River. islands away. I come here in these little boys, jump over the truck, go to the island, say, go down to Shell Beach, go down to Mouth of the River, go down to Boyle Woods. We used to catch that train here in Allogies. They call it the Shell Beach. Shell Beach train. Yes. No, this is Shell Beach over here, the Grand Island. That's a train in Allogies. Before they broke it up, you understand, we used to have coaches. We used to catch it to the Burris. As we go to Burris, we catch a mail boat. Oh, go by boat for a while. Yeah, we go to Burris. After we get to Burris, we play a tune and we catch the mail boat and we get on hit there about six o'clock in the evening. Now it looked like it's almost as far from Burris as here. Burris here. Yeah, on the mail boat. Was that the Grand Isle? That's the Grand Isle. That's the Grand Isle. Yeah. We used to go down there and play.
